body.statement: For the parameter \(K_G\) as defined, the literal parameterized problem is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete already at \(k=0\).  More precisely, the restriction of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) to the instances satisfying \(K_G=0\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete.  Hence \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\) cannot yield an \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\) algorithm for the class stated in the question unless \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).  This conclusion uses singularity-preserving fiber bijections and no genericity assumption.
body.proof_tex:
Membership follows from the same universal formula used for \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\): for two supported matrices satisfying all missing-edge equations, their queried entries must be equal.  This formula has polynomial size independently of the maximum indegree, so the promised restriction belongs to \(\forall\mathbb R\).

For hardness, start with the depth-one compiler in the fan-in-two completeness theorem.  For each coefficient sink \(v\) having exactly two private parents, add a fresh private root \(r_v\) and the edge \(r_v\to v\), with new coefficient \(u_v\).  Add a fresh zero-parent vertex \(w_v\) and make \(\{v,w_v\}\) a missing bidirected pair.  Program its equation as
\[
\Omega_{v,w_v}=u_v=0
\]
by setting \(\Sigma_{v,w_v}=0\), \(\Sigma_{r_v,w_v}=-1\), and \(\Sigma_{a,w_v}=0\) for the two old parents \(a\) of \(v\).  In every inherited missing-pair equation involving \(v\), set all newly appearing covariance slots involving \(r_v\) to zero.  The inherited residual is then unchanged, while the new residual forces \(u_v=0\).

Declare all other new pairs bidirected, retain the old programmed off-diagonal slots, set unspecified off-diagonal slots to zero, and reset every diagonal to
\[
1+\max_i\sum_{j\ne i}|\Sigma_{ij}|.
\]
Exactly as in the compiler proof, the resulting rational symmetric matrix is strictly diagonally dominant and positive definite.  No residual uses a diagonal entry because the graph remains depth one and all equation endpoints are distinct.

Projection that deletes the new coefficients maps the padded fiber to the original fiber.  Its inverse inserts \(u_v=0\) for every padded sink.  The preceding residual calculations prove that these maps are mutually inverse; in particular, the queried-coordinate attainable set is unchanged and singular branches are neither removed nor added.  Every former indegree-two sink now has indegree three, every other old sink has indegree at most one, and every new vertex has indegree zero.  Therefore the padded graph has maximum indegree three and
\[
K_G=|\{v:|\operatorname{pa}_D(v)|=2\}|=0.
\]
The padding has polynomial size and preserves the rational planted feasible point by adjoining zeros.  Composing it with the promise reduction from \(\mathsf{coSEL\mbox{-}PNQF}\) proves \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hardness at \(k=0\), and membership proves completeness.  Thus the parameter, as literally defined without a maximum-indegree-two restriction, does not measure distance from the fan-in-one class.
